findings.title: File access editor silently completes when receipt contradicts requested restriction

steps: Open client Files and Manage access for Test report.pdf.
Select Specific people with no selected users (UI says uploader-only).
Submit PATCH {viewerMode:'restricted',viewerUserIds:[]} to the file access endpoint.
Return the original same-ID fixture with viewerMode:'all',viewerUserIds:[]; keep subsequent list/roster reads unchanged.
reproduction.actual: Editor closes, no alert is shown, and no assertion requires returned viewerMode/viewerUserIds to match the requested restriction.
reproduction.expected: Retain the review and expose a conflicting or unverified result until exact requested ACL is acknowledged. A same-ID response alone is insufficient.

findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks acceptance of file access management and is recommended as a release blocker for a product exposing this control. No cross-tenant disclosure or backend authorization bypass was demonstrated; the confirmed risk is false completion of a confidentiality change.

findings.title: Folder change discards the draft when the same-ID receipt still names the old folder

steps: Select Test report.pdf in Reports; click New folder.
Enter Reviewed destination, submit PATCH {folder:'Reviewed destination'}.
Return the same file with folder:'Reports'; list readback also remains Reports.
reproduction.actual: Dialog closes and no error appears; Reports remains in the table.
reproduction.expected: Keep the requested folder draft and flag unverified/conflicting confirmation.

findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks row acceptance for verified move/new-folder saves. Distinct from the known absence of atomic multi-file moves.

findings.title: Ambiguous file deletion response immediately re-enables the destructive confirmation

steps: Open Delete file for Test report.pdf and confirm.
Return HTTP 503 after the DELETE was dispatched.
reproduction.actual: The button is enabled immediately and a second DELETE is sent. The dialog has a generic failure only and no unknown-outcome state/reconciliation.
reproduction.expected: Disclose that the dispatched outcome is unknown and require current-state/operation reconciliation before presenting a renewed destructive intent.

findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks acceptance of interrupted-delete recovery. The browser proves repeat dispatch only; backend idempotency and duplicate effects were not tested. Lower priority than CP-01.

findings.title: Facilities entry opens a standalone editor instead of the designed management dialog

steps: Load overview with the existing synthetic facility fixture.
Click the plus Add facility control in District nexus.
reproduction.actual: A 640px standalone Add facility form opens; the existing facility list, inline Edit/Remove controls and inline geocode candidates are absent from this dialog. State is a free-text input and address fields use the generic two-column grid.
reproduction.expected: Figma 411:58068/58269 specifies a 700px Facilities: client manager with saved facility cards above an inline add/edit form, City/State/ZIP in three columns, and footer Add facility/Done.

findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks exact design/workflow acceptance for the facility manager, not the validity of existing guarded add/edit/geocode adapters. Recomposition is frontend work; provider/native qualification stays separate. The map error visible behind this capture is an intentionally unstubbed fixture contract and is not a product finding.

findings.title: Overview timeline retains a generic dot list instead of the designed grouped activity feed

steps: Open overview with one recorded note in the existing activity contract.
Compare timeline markup and capture against full context for 411:48826.
reproduction.actual: Each item uses the same grey dot/vertical connector, raw kind on a separate line and full timestamp. CSS limits the internal list to 420px. No date-group headers or kind-specific icon tiles are rendered.
reproduction.expected: The supplied default timeline has dated groups, 70px bordered feed rows, 32px kind icon tiles, compact metadata and row-level status/action positions. Expanded dialog 411:60193 is also not mounted by the current overview.

findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks exact timeline visual acceptance. Existing filtering and guarded actions remain independently implemented; no pagination or native-history completeness is claimed.
findings.evidenceLimit: The 411:48826 and 411:49157 child raster exports are ancestor-clipped. Dated group/icon/70px row geometry is established by full returned design context; 411:60524 supplies an unobscured timeline visual. The owner-excluded Open commitments summary is not part of this defect.

findings.title: Files toolbar and results header do not follow the supplied Files composition

steps: Open client Files with the existing two-file fixture and wait for fonts/table.
reproduction.actual: Source and sort are adjacent native selects after search; result count and Move to folder form a detached toolbar above the table. The table has no enclosing folder header/breadcrumb or Upload here action. The alternate Folders card-grid view shown in 411:53189 is also absent; only the sidebar/table view is implemented.
reproduction.expected: Figma uses an inline source-chip row, right-aligned Sort Created, and a table card with folder breadcrumb/name/count and Upload here header. Differences in fixture file count, names and unavailable quotas are excluded from this finding.

findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks exact Files presentation acceptance. Smart-link composition and source-taxonomy definitions remain separate owner dependencies; do not invent unavailable records/categories.
